name: Chin-Jaw Detail
description: Inspects geometric precision and texture continuity along chin-jaw contours where face-swap boundaries commonly create detectable discontinuities, following FaceForensics++ forensic methodology.
mechanism:
This method analyzes chin and jawline detail for deepfake detection:

1. **Jawline Contour Extraction**: Facial landmarks along the mandible and chin are tracked per frame to extract the jawline contour. The contour is parameterized using curvature measures, capturing the anatomical shape signature unique to each individual.

2. **Sub-Mandibular Region Analysis**: The region beneath the chin and along the jawline is examined for anatomical detail — skin folds, adipose tissue distribution, and the chin-neck junction. These areas are challenging for deepfake generators because they occur at the boundary of the face-swap region and often exhibit generation artifacts.

3. **Temporal Contour Stability**: The jawline contour is tracked across frames during speech and head movement. Natural jawlines deform smoothly according to musculoskeletal constraints — the mandible rotates on the temporomandibular joint with predictable kinematics. Deepfake-generated jawlines may exhibit unnatural deformations, warping, or contour instability.

4. **Jaw-Neck Boundary Coherence**: The boundary between the face-generated region and the original neck/body is a critical artifact location for face-swap deepfakes. The method analyzes texture, color, and geometric continuity at this boundary — discontinuities indicate where the generated face mesh fails to blend seamlessly with the original body.

5. **Detail Resolution Assessment**: Fine details along the jawline (stubble, skin texture, moles) are analyzed for rendering quality and temporal consistency. Deepfake generators often produce lower-resolution detail in peripheral face regions (chin, jaw) compared to central regions (eyes, nose), creating a detectable detail gradient.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through chin-jaw detail analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Rossler, A. et al. (2019). FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images. ICCV.
Li, Y. et al. (2020). Face X-ray for More General Face Forgery Detection. CVPR.
